b: I need help from those who know more than I.

We had our stairs remodeled for not an insignificant amount of money. I had discussed with the contractor before the project started that I wanted the baseboard/trim to be consistent throughout the steps and I didn’t like how it stopped at the step while other steps had the trim connecting to the next step. I recognize there was room for miscommunication there.

Fast forward to the completion of the project (we didn’t walk through it together before painting started or anything like that- I would just check the stairs when the contractor was busy doing something else), so I missed this before the painting was done.
So I send pictures to the project manager because he never came by for a final inspection or walkthrough with me and I said I didn’t like how the two middle steps done have the trim connect.

The woman who manages all the projects called me and said it couldn’t be done. I explained that I didn’t understand why that couldn’t be done but recognize my knowledge is limited. However, this really doesn’t seem like it should be a problem. Everything I’m reading online is confirming my suspicions but I want to make sure I’m not in an echo chamber

I just want to say so far working with them has been pretty good. They are very nice and flexible and the craftsmanship so far has been really great. But this part is confusing me. It doesn’t seem like it should be that hard to do.
I haven’t paid the final payment yet because I want more answers and clarification on this aspect before making the payment.
EDIT: wow thanks everyone for responding! (Except that one guy that said I was complaining when I’m asking for advice).

Also- I thought the overall craftsmanship was done well. Maybe that’s because they were done so poorly before by the previous owner? But we paid $5.6k for this work and I thought, besides the trim question, it was done well. Was I blind to the quality?
EDIT ^2: there is a warranty clause in the contract for defects in craftsmanship and installation
